title: Simple Method for Pinpointing Specific Osmium-Fixed Cells in Culture for SEM
content: Array tomography within the Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) is a powerful technique for understanding cell-cell interactions at high resolution and in 3-dimensions. However, the volume sampled can be quite small compared to the entire specimen volume, creating a “needle-in-a-haystack problem” when trying to locate specific regions of interest. To make matters worse, samples become opaque when processed for SEM using heavy-metal staining protocols making through-focal imaging of the resin block nearly impossible. The researcher could iteratively prepare ribbon sections, screen the sections within the SEM for the interaction of interest, and then go back to the ultramicrotome if no suitable location has yet to be sectioned. However, this approach is tedious, time-consuming, and often costly. Here we aimed to develop a more efficient, less costly method to pinpoint cell-cell interactions in cell culture.
